newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares mixed, Maybank leads blue chip gains.
newsitem.headline: KL shares mixed, Maybank leads blue chip gains.

text.p: Shares were mixed in early morning trade, with Maybank leading continued gains for blue chips, dealers said on Tuesday.

They said activities remained centered on second-tier main board shares with profit taking holding back the second board counters. "There's more interest on second board and second liners, most of it from retail and Singapore investors," said a local brokerage dealer.
At around 0225 GMT, the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks was up 2.55 points to 1,238.24.
The Second Board index of smaller issues eased 1.34 to 604.35.

Most-active KL Industries notched another year-high, rising 17 cents to 5.10 on speculative buying. The property and consumer products stock, which is also traded in Singapore, was actively bidded in the island republic.
Olympia, back from a two-week suspension, surged 22 cents to 2.44. The property and gaming firm announced on Monday it was buying a prime piece of property for 750 million ringgit.
Top commercial bank, Maybank rose 50 cents to 27.50, close to a 12-month high of 28.00.
